name: bounded environment-sensitive translation-validation certificate checker

public_basis.finding: Reproducibility is relative to build tools/versions/OS assumptions; same source alone is not enough and verification normally rebuilds/compares outputs.
A compiler run can be checked after the fact by validating that produced target preserves source semantics.
A producer can attach a machine-checkable proof that the consumer validates against its policy; verification can be much smaller than trusting production.

fail_reasons: environment blob SHA differs from certificate
PUSH_ENV bound value 5 differs from current binding 6
stale final claim 36 differs from source+environment result 39

negative_controls.reason: target no longer equals syntax-directed compilation of source
12*3=36 so transition and final claim disagree
DIV is outside closed rule set; verifier fails closed rather than extrapolating semantics

what_was_eliminated: For this closed finite language, no external compiler, VM, CI service, package build, user execution or hosted compute is needed to validate the compilation/test outcome; the verifier checks a finite source/environment/target/trace relation directly in Chat-visible text.
what_was_not_eliminated: This does not compile or validate arbitrary real toolchains. General translation validation can itself require a verifier program/theorem prover, and proof/certificate production for unrestricted source may require external computation. Reproducibility metadata alone does not prove an artifact without an actual rebuild or stronger certificate.
scope: Closed EnvExpr-v1/Stack-v1 with const/env/add/mul signed-64 semantics and one explicit environment binding. No general compiler correctness or arbitrary program equivalence claim.
